name: CNSA 1.0 (transitional suite)
reference: NSA CSA 'Announcing the Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0' (U/OO/194427-22, PP-22-1338, September 2022), Table V: CNSA 1.0 algorithms.
summary: The classical NSA suite that national security systems run today while migrating to CNSA 2.0. Achievable with current SSH software, unlike CNSA 2.0.

kex.reason: Table V: ECDH over Curve P-384. ecdh-sha2-nistp384 is the only SSH key exchange whose transcript hash is SHA-384; the SHA-512 MODP methods are not listed.

host_key.reason: Table V: ECDSA over Curve P-384 with SHA-384, which is exactly ecdsa-sha2-nistp384. SSH has no rsa-sha2-384, so no SSH RSA signature uses the required hash.

cipher.reason: Table V: AES with 256-bit keys. Every SSH spelling of AES-256 qualifies; the table names the primitive, not an SSH registration.

mac.reason: Table V names SHA-384. SSH has no HMAC-SHA-384, so the only integrity over a CNSA-approved construction is the AES-256-GCM tag. A server advertising any HMAC does not conform.

notes: CNSA 1.0 Table V pins primitives and parameters, not SSH identifiers, and reads 'Use SHA-384 for all classification levels' literally: an algorithm is listed only if the hash it uses is SHA-384, with no substitution and nothing imported from CNSA 2.0. That makes the conforming set very small, and the honest consequence is that no stock OpenSSH server passes this profile: (1) the only key exchange whose transcript hash is SHA-384 is ecdh-sha2-nistp384 -- the diffie-hellman-group*-sha512 methods use SHA-512, so they are not listed even though their modulus meets the 3072-bit floor; (2) the only signature is ecdsa-sha2-nistp384 (P-384 with SHA-384); SSH has no rsa-sha2-384, so no SSH RSA signature uses the required hash; (3) AES-256 is the cipher (any SSH spelling, since CNSA names the primitive, not an RFC registration); (4) the only integrity is the AES-256-GCM tag, because SSH has no HMAC-SHA-384 and a real sshd always advertises an HMAC that uses another hash, which fails the allowlist. Reporting that gap is the point rather than papering over it with a SHA-512 stand-in.
